Treatment Summary
The patient presented following a motor vehicle collision in which their vehicle was struck from the side while turning left. The
reported mechanism, including the nature and force of the impact, is consistent with the cervical injury diagnosed, which is
whiplash-type soft tissue trauma to the neck and upper back. Care was delivered over 23 visits and followed a typical course of
rehabilitation: ealry visits focused on pain control and getnle range-of-motion work, with progressive strengthening added as
symptoms eased. Visit frequency tapered steadily as the patient improved and reported less pain and stiffness.
Examination findings are mixed. Palpation revealed muscle guarding and reduced cervical range of motion, which support the
injury, while several neurological screening tests returned normal results. The patient reports a remote history of a minor strain in
the same region several years ago, which resolved completely without lasting limitation. Billing records reflect single,
appropriate charges for each service rendered, with no duplicate or repeated entries.
At discharge the patient was improving, with residual stiffness expected to resolve with a home exercise program.
